claims.statement: The Mój Prąd application workflow calls for multiple electronic documents, and the official instructions state that lack of the OSD connection certificate causes rejection; documentation completeness is therefore tied to a concrete loss event.

The proposed payer is the installer operations owner because the service is intended to reduce commissioning rework and protect collection or after-sales economics; actual willingness to pay is not yet evidenced.
The founder can request, but cannot presume, a written nonexclusive pilot workflow agreement from the parents' installer and can replace a refusal by recruiting an unrelated installer.
URE reported more than 1.6 million prosumer microinstallations in Poland at the end of 2025, indicating a large installed base but not proving demand for this product.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Owner or operations manager responsible for commissioning quality and callbacks
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Cross-brand rules, neutral audit trails, and portability across installers must be materially better than a bundled vendor checklist
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The installer retains its homeowner relationship; the founder company contracts directly only with the installer
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: A separately consented family-firm pilot, followed by unrelated installers, wholesalers, and trade-software partners

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Founder-led outbound and distributor referrals; target CAC below three months of gross profit, unvalidated
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Prepaid passport bundles or monthly card/invoice billing; target cash before or within 14 days of delivery
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Target 65-80% after automation; unvalidated until manual-review rates are observed
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Remote onboarding, checklist updates, and installer support; no field installation labor
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Legal review, processor agreements, security controls, insurance, and rule-update monitoring
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 120-250 PLN per completed passport plus 300-900 PLN monthly account fee
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Document storage, OCR, messaging, and occasional manual exception review

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Installer CRMs, equipment vendors, or subsidy consultants could add document checklists and bundle them cheaply
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: A completed installation creates a concrete documentation event; missing required evidence can cause application rejection, rework, delayed payment, or a harder warranty defense
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: First rejected or incomplete subsidy/grid packet, repeated handover rework, or a distributor requiring standardized commissioning evidence
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Monthly platform renewal or purchase of the next block of commissioning passports

contrary_evidence: Installers may already use adequate CRM templates, shared drives, or manufacturer apps at near-zero marginal cost.
The cited Mój Prąd intake had closed, so its precise document set cannot be treated as a permanent demand source.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Nonexclusive 12-month workflow-integration and data-processing agreement limited to opted-in installations
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Pilot with any unrelated installer using the same standalone mobile handover flow
critical_control_point.current_owner: Each independent installer controls its own workflow and customer records
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The installer retains its homeowner relationship; the founder company contracts directly only with the installer
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The parents' approximately seven-person renewable installer can be approached for a lawful voluntary pilot, but the founder has no assumed ownership, customer rights, data rights, or contracting authority and must obtain written consent.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: A willing installer and the founder company jointly after written opt-in; the family firm remains independently controlled
critical_control_point.subject: Opt-in digital checkpoint in the installer's commissioning and handover workflow

economics.acquisition_route: One opt-in operating-relationship pilot, then direct sales and nonexclusive distributor referrals
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, not forecast: 400 installers averaging 12 passports monthly at 170 PLN implies about 9.8m PLN annual revenue; durable margins and a saleable software asset would still need proof to support a 5m PLN founder outcome
economics.founder_time: Initial build and five pilots within five hours per day alongside employment; support must be scheduled, not on-call
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software-led document validation with manual work restricted to exceptions
economics.payback: Target under three months on installer CAC; not yet validated
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 120-250 PLN per installation plus 300-900 PLN per installer per month
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeats with every installation and renews if rules, records, and warranty evidence stay useful

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Consented, de-identified exception patterns improve document checks by device, grid operator, and program version
fingerprint.customer: Small Polish photovoltaic, battery, and heat-pump installers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Begin with a voluntarily contracted pilot at the parents' independently owned installer, then sell the same workflow to unrelated installers and equipment distributors
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: White-label mobile evidence capture, rules-based completeness checks, and an immutable customer handover pack sold per installation plus a small platform fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays when a commissioning passport is completed and optionally renews a portfolio subscription
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A residential installation reaches commissioning but its acceptance, device, payment, grid, or subsidy evidence is incomplete or scattered

founder_fit: Rules, document extraction, and anomaly detection match data-science strengths
A narrow automated workflow can be operated in under five founder hours per day after onboarding
The lawful family operating relationship permits fast problem discovery without assuming rights to the firm or its customers
Per-install usage and rejection rates are measurable
risks: Changing subsidy and grid rules can make checks stale
Personal-data or cybersecurity failures could create disproportionate liability
Crew noncompliance could erase the benefit
A pilot at the family firm may not generalize to unrelated installers

structure.commercial_archetype: Per-commissioning productized evidence service with optional recurring portfolio access
structure.control_point: The documented sign-off checkpoint immediately before installer-to-customer handover
structure.critical_dependency: Installer adoption of the capture workflow and accurate maintenance of changing document rules

thesis: Acquire an opt-in position in an installer's commissioning workflow and sell a per-install digital evidence passport that validates required handover, subsidy, grid, and warranty documents before the crew closes the job.
title: Commissioning Passport Rail for Small Renewable Installers
uncertainties: Frequency and cost of document-driven rework across small installers
Whether homeowners will consent to an additional processor holding installation records
Which installer system integrations are necessary for repeated use
Achievable price before installers revert to manual checklists
